\section{Domain Model}
Figure~\ref{ch5:fig:domain} shows the concepts FlakeTrace works with and how they relate. Each
box uses the name the concept has in the code, shown in brackets. The figure is drawn from the
three contracts in \texttt{docs/contracts/} and from the data classes in \texttt{eval/baseline.py}
and \texttt{runner/diagnose.py}.

A \emph{diagnosis} starts from one failing test, the \emph{victim}, in a Maven project. Member~2's
runner executes \emph{test orders}. Each \emph{run} uses one fresh JVM and runs the tests in
exactly the given order, and every test in the order gets an \emph{outcome}. A failed outcome
carries a \emph{failure signature}: the exception type and a normalised stack trace. The message is
kept but not compared (\texttt{FailureSignature.matches}), because it can change from run to run
for the same bug. The first real failure of the victim becomes the diagnosis's \emph{reference}
signature, and later runs count only failures that match it. Every run is one line of the
\emph{execution record}, and the project's files are hashed before and after the diagnosis
(\emph{source integrity}), because FlakeTrace must not change the code it analyses.

My module adds the explanation. A test makes \emph{accesses} to a \emph{shared resource}, either a
static field or a system property with a constant key, by reading or writing it at a bytecode
location. Each access also records which root it was reached from (for example a \texttt{@Before}
method) and how many calls deep it is. An \emph{edge} pairs one polluter write with one victim read
of the same resource. It is the mechanism the report names. When the runner finds several
polluters, each one is analysed as a separate pair with the victim. Finally, Member~3's
\emph{report} concludes the diagnosis with an outcome and, if it is unresolved, a typed reason.

\begin{figure}[H]\centering

  \caption{Domain model of one order-dependence diagnosis}\label{ch5:fig:domain}
\end{figure}
\section{Data Design}
FlakeTrace keeps no database. Its data is three kinds of file, one per stage of a diagnosis
(Table~\ref{ch5:tab:datastores}). The diagnosis report is the one all three members write into,
so its structure is shown in Figure~\ref{ch5:fig:datamodel}, drawn only from
\texttt{eval/schema/report.schema.json}.

\begin{table}[H]\centering\small\setlength{\tabcolsep}{4pt}
\begin{tabular}{>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.16\textwidth}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.36\textwidth}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.19\textwidth}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.2\textwidth}}
\toprule
Data & Format & Written by & Defined in \\
\midrule
Resource evidence & JSON: Output 1 (accesses per test) and Output 2 (edges for one pair) & \nolinkurl{evidence/extract.py} (M1) & Resource-evidence contract (\nolinkurl{docs/contracts/}) \\
Execution record & JSON lines: a header (victim, $n$, Java version, project commit, OS, shuffle settings), then one line per JVM run (step, order, every test's outcome and signature, time) & \nolinkurl{runner/recording.py} (M2) & ADR-004 \\
Diagnosis report & One JSON file per victim, \texttt{<record>.report.json}, validated against the schema & \nolinkurl{eval/report.py}, saved by \nolinkurl{runner/cli.py} & Report schema (\nolinkurl{eval/schema/}) \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\caption{The data FlakeTrace stores for one diagnosis}\label{ch5:tab:datastores}
\end{table}

\paragraph{The report.} A report describes one victim. It has 17 required fields and one optional
field, \texttt{order\_exploration}, added by ADR-008. Each field in Figure~\ref{ch5:fig:datamodel}
is tagged with the member who fills it, following the field table in
\texttt{docs/contracts/report-schema.md}. Member~2's runner supplies the tests, the orders, the
reference failure signature, the source-integrity result and the pointer to the execution record.
Member~3 turns the runner's raw counts into Wilson intervals and decides \texttt{outcome} and
\texttt{unresolved\_reason}. My module fills \texttt{shared\_resource},
\texttt{polluter\_write\_location} and \texttt{victim\_read\_location} through
\texttt{report\_fields} (Section~\ref{ch5:sec:process}), and adds its limitation lines.

\paragraph{Rules the schema enforces.} \texttt{unresolved\_reason} must be set exactly when the
outcome is \texttt{UNRESOLVED}. \texttt{failure\_signature} is null exactly when the reason is
\texttt{NOT\_REPRODUCED} or \texttt{INFRASTRUCTURE\_FAILURE}: nothing ever failed for a real
reason, so there is no real signature to report. No other fields are allowed. Every report is
checked by \texttt{validate\_report} (\texttt{eval/schema\_validator.py}) before it is saved. The
rule that \texttt{VERIFIED} needs a resource edge is not in the schema; it is enforced by
\texttt{decide()} in \texttt{eval/outcome.py}.

\paragraph{A real example.} In \texttt{eval/reports/f2.json} (fixture case F2), the runner reduced
an order of 6 tests to 2: \texttt{FeaturePolluterTest\#enableTurbo}, then the victim
\texttt{FeatureVictimTest\#expectsTurboDisabled}. My fields say the shared resource is the system
property \texttt{odfixture.turbo}, written in \texttt{enableTurbo} at bytecode offset 4 and read in
\texttt{FeatureFlags.isTurboEnabled} at offset 2, a helper one call below the test. The pair
reproduced the failure 20 times out of 20 (Wilson lower bound 0.839) and the victim never failed
alone (0/20), so the outcome is \texttt{VERIFIED}.

\paragraph{Limitations.} The report holds one resource and one write and read location. Any other
edge is only named in \texttt{limitations}; for example, \texttt{f3.json} shows \texttt{flagA} and
names \texttt{flagB} there. The execution records themselves are not committed to the repository
(\texttt{eval/reports/README.md}); each report keeps only the path to its record.

\section{Process / Behavior Design}\label{ch5:sec:process}
Four diagrams describe what happens in one diagnosis, in the order it happens:
\begin{itemize}
\item who calls whom (Figure~\ref{ch5:fig:diagnose-seq}, Member~2);
\item which test orders are run and when the search stops (Figure~\ref{ch5:fig:search-activity},
  Member~2);
\item how my module finds the shared resource (Figure~\ref{ch5:fig:evidence-dfd});
\item how the outcome is decided (Figure~\ref{ch5:fig:outcome}, Member~3).
\end{itemize}
Each diagram shows only what is implemented on \texttt{main}, and each was drawn from the code
named in its own source file under \nolinkurl{mid-eval-report/diagrams/}.

\subsection{The \texttt{diagnose} command}
Figure~\ref{ch5:fig:diagnose-seq} follows one run of
\texttt{py -m runner diagnose -{}-project <dir> -{}-victim Class\#method}. The command first checks
its input; a malformed victim, a missing \texttt{pom.xml} or a bad \texttt{-{}-order} file stops it
with exit code~2. \texttt{diagnose()} then hashes every project file, finds the project's tests by
running the harness once with \texttt{-{}-list}, and starts the execution record with its header
line. Every run after that goes through \texttt{RecordingRunner}: a fresh JVM runs the given order
from standard input, and every test's outcome is appended to the record as one line. After the
last run the files are hashed again and compared. Only when polluters were found does the command
call my \texttt{analyse\_pair}, once per polluter, and combine the results. Member~3's
\texttt{assemble\_report} then decides the outcome, validates the report and writes it next to the
record (exit~0). A failing Maven or Java call, or an error in my extractor, gives exit~1. The one
status that still produces no report, \texttt{NO\_SINGLE\_POLLUTER}, gives exit~3.

\subsection{Reproduce, search, minimise, verify}
Figure~\ref{ch5:fig:search-activity} is \texttt{run\_steps} in \nolinkurl{runner/diagnose.py}. It
runs five phases:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Reproduce.} The starting order runs up to $n$ times and stops at the first real
  failure, whose signature becomes the reference. A crash, timeout or skip never counts as a
  reproduction.
\item \textbf{Shuffle} (ADR-008). If nothing failed, up to 31 distinct shuffled orders are tried,
  one run each. Classes are shuffled first, then the methods inside each class, so methods of
  different classes are never mixed, which JUnit itself would not do. Each order's seed is
  recorded. Fixture F4 was found this way: \nolinkurl{eval/reports/f4.json} records the
  reproducing seed~1 after 2 shuffled orders. Fixture N3 never failed in any of 31 shuffled
  orders, so its report is \texttt{NOT\_REPRODUCED}.
\item \textbf{Alone.} The victim runs alone $n$ times. A matching failure means it fails without
  any polluter.
\item \textbf{Search, then minimise} (ADR-007). Each earlier test is run once as
  \texttt{[candidate, victim]}. If no single test is enough, the full order runs once more, and
  only if it fails again does delta debugging (\texttt{ddmin}) shrink the earlier tests to a set
  in which removing any one test stops the failure (1-minimal, not necessarily the smallest). For
  F3 this reduced 15 tests to the 2 polluters plus the victim (\nolinkurl{eval/reports/f3.json}).
\item \textbf{Verify.} The polluters plus the victim run $n$ times, counting the runs that fail
  with the reference signature and the runs that fail for any reason.
\end{enumerate}

% Search pipeline activity (M2): diagrams/m2/search_activity.puml
\begin{figure}[p]\centering
  \includegraphics[width=\textwidth,height=0.85\textheight,keepaspectratio]{figures/m2/search_activity}
  \caption{Reproduce, polluter search, minimisation and verification}\label{ch5:fig:search-activity}
\end{figure}

\subsection{Static evidence extraction}
Figure~\ref{ch5:fig:evidence-dfd} is my module, \nolinkurl{evidence/extract.py}, as one call to
\texttt{analyse\_pair}. For the polluter and then the victim, \texttt{find\_roots} collects the test
method and every lifecycle method that runs with it, including inherited ones and the test class's
static initialiser. From each root a breadth-first walk reads the compiled classes with
\texttt{javap}, one class at a time and cached, and looks at every bytecode instruction:
\begin{itemize}
\item \texttt{getstatic} and \texttt{putstatic} become static-field reads and writes;
\item the system-property calls become reads and writes when the key is a constant string;
\item calls into the project's own classes are followed one level deeper;
\item calls into the JDK or libraries are only listed;
\item anything else the extractor cannot model becomes a typed unsupported observation.
\end{itemize}
\texttt{find\_edges} then keeps the resources that the polluter writes and the victim reads. If
there is no edge but some walk stopped at the depth limit, the pair is analysed again one level
deeper, up to depth~5 (ADR-006). Finally \texttt{report\_fields} turns the first edge into the three
report fields and names everything else in \texttt{limitations}.

An empty result sets \texttt{no\_supported\_resource\_evidence}; it never means the two tests are
independent. The data flow also shows the extractor's limits: it reads only compiled classes and
never runs a test, so a write that the polluter restores later is still reported as a write.

% Evidence extraction data flow (M1): diagrams/m1/evidence_dataflow.puml
\begin{figure}[p]\centering
  \includegraphics[height=0.85\textheight]{figures/m1/evidence_dataflow}
  \caption{Static evidence extraction: from bytecode to resource edges}\label{ch5:fig:evidence-dfd}
\end{figure}

\subsection{Outcome decision}
Figure~\ref{ch5:fig:outcome} is \texttt{decide()} in \nolinkurl{eval/outcome.py}. The rules are
checked from top to bottom and the first one that matches decides:
\begin{enumerate}
\item failed source integrity means nothing can be trusted;
\item a victim that fails alone cannot be blamed on a polluter;
\item if the reduced sequence never failed with the reference signature, the reason says why:
  \texttt{NOT\_REPRODUCED}, \texttt{INFRASTRUCTURE\_FAILURE} (only crashes or timeouts) or
  \texttt{SIGNATURE\_MISMATCH} (a different real failure);
\item without a resource edge the result is \texttt{UNRESOLVED} with the reason
  \texttt{NO\_\allowbreak SUPPORTED\_\allowbreak RESOURCE\_\allowbreak EVIDENCE};
\item \texttt{VERIFIED} needs both an edge and a Wilson lower bound of at least 0.70; otherwise the
  result is \texttt{CANDIDATE}.
\end{enumerate}
With $n = 20$, 20 reproductions out of 20 give a lower bound of 0.839, which is what F1--F4 reached.
